Independent sign off

Air monitoring and clearance certificates, issued independently

Air monitoring during and after asbestos removal, and the clearance certificate that lets the next stage of work begin. Carried out by a licensed asbestos assessor who is independent of the removalist and independent of us. That independence is the point of it. Tell us when removal finishes, and we will book the independent assessor for the clearance.

0456 220 552

Removal by licensed asbestos removalists. Max holds demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Removal scope confirmed

    Who Max, with the removalist

    The assessor needs to know what was removed and from where, in order to clear it.

  2. 02

    Independent assessor engaged

    Who Max

    Engaged separately from the removalist. The person checking the work cannot be the person who did it.

  3. 03

    Monitoring plan

    Who The assessor

    Where the monitors sit and how often. On friable work monitoring runs throughout, not only at the end.

  4. 04

    Area cleaned and prepared

    Who The licensed removalist

    Clearance is not a formality. If the visual inspection fails, the cleaning repeats before anything is sampled.

  5. 05

    Visual inspection

    Who The assessor

    Before any clearance air monitoring, the area is inspected for visible residue and debris.

  6. 06

    Certificate issued

    Who The assessor

    Issued to you. Keep it: it is the document that proves the area was cleared.

The detail

What the certificate actually means

  • It is specific to the area removed. Not the whole building, not the whole property. The boundary of the clearance is the boundary of the removal.
  • It is issued by an independent party. A licensed asbestos assessor, not the removalist and not the demolisher. Independence is what makes it worth anything.
  • It follows a visual inspection first. If there is visible debris, nothing is sampled until the area is cleaned again.
  • On friable work it follows continuous monitoring. The air is monitored throughout the removal as well as at the end.
  • It is the gate for the next stage. Demolition does not begin, and a building is not reoccupied, until it is issued.
  • It outlives the job. Keep it with the disposal dockets. Together they are what proves the property was handled properly.

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Clearance is what lets the machine start

On a knockdown, the clearance certificate is the gate between the asbestos work and the demolition. It is why the survey happens first and why the sequence cannot be reordered.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Who issues the clearance certificate?
A licensed asbestos assessor, independent of the removalist and of us. We arrange and coordinate them, but we do not and cannot issue it ourselves.
Do I always need one?
For friable removal, yes. For bonded removal it depends on the scale and the circumstances of the work. We will tell you which applies to your job rather than selling you one you do not need.
What if the clearance fails?
The area is cleaned again by the removalist and re-inspected. Nothing proceeds until it passes. That is the whole function of having an independent check.
How long does clearance take?
The visual inspection is quick. The air monitoring has a sampling period and a laboratory turnaround, and that is what sets the timing. It is worth building into the programme rather than assuming it is same day.
Should I keep the certificate?
Yes, with the disposal dockets. A future purchaser, certifier or lender may ask for both, and reproducing them after the fact is not possible.

Get a quote

Ask us where clearance sits in your programme

On most jobs the clearance is the gate between the asbestos work and everything after it. Knowing when it lands is usually more useful than knowing what it costs.
